My job is to ask one question about every sentence that reaches me. Not is it true. Who is saying it, and would they say it with their name on.
And in the case we are discussing, the answer was nobody.
The answer was a screenshot. Which is not a source, however many times it circulates.
The other paper would say it only reported that a claim existed. That is true, and it feels like an evasion.
Because it is both. The existence of a claim is a fact and reporting it is legitimate. What is not legitimate is doing it in language that reads like confirmation.
So the grammar is the ethics. It is said that is doing work that a plain sentence would not get away with.
That is exactly it, and it took me fifteen years to be able to say it that clearly. We use those structures every day, and once a week one of them is a hiding place.
How do you tell the difference? Because from outside it reads identically.

Now to a claim that has been circulating since the weekend. It is said that a senior official attended a meeting last month that he was not authorised to attend, and he is believed to have arrived after it had begun. A source close to the department, speaking on condition of anonymity, has confirmed that the meeting took place, though not who was present. The claim originated in a private message which has since been widely shared, and it remains unsubstantiated. No evidence has been produced, and the department is understood to be preparing a statement. We have asked the official's office for comment and have not so far received one. We will bring you more as we have it.

Here are the tests I actually apply, and they are less impressive than people expect. First, for an anonymous source: I have to know who it is, personally, and somebody else in this building has to be able to confirm that the person is who they say they are. Anonymous to the reader is fine. Anonymous to me is not a source, it is a rumour with a better font. Second, I will not run the phrase it is widely reported that, when the reports being referred to are all quoting each other. That sentence is a circle and it is doing the job of evidence without being evidence. And third, a thing that took me years to understand. Official silence lends credence. Every time. People who refuse to comment believe they are staying out of the story, and what they are actually doing is removing the only thing that could have stopped it.
